note: Faithful rendering of the commentary on the dhyāna similes and the water-source glosses; terms (vitarka/vicāra, adhyātmasaṃprasāda) handled acceptably.

errors.english: suppose there were two men who were extremely fierce
errors.why: The sutra introduces a second man (a second illustration after the robber of the previous example), not a pair of men of whom one acts; 'that man' (མི་དེས) then refers to him.

note: Accurate translation of the Kāśyapaparivarta passage on accepting alms without attainment; only the framing of the new simile is slightly off.

errors.english: The knowledge of karma, results, and other cognitions would become possible for just anyone; it would not remain merely partial knowledge, because that would lead to an absurd consequence.
errors.why: The objection is that whatever establishes the possibility of knowing karma and its results would also establish other knowledge, so the teacher's knowledge would not be merely partial, on pain of over-extension; 'for just anyone' is not in the Tibetan.

errors.english: Showing how omniscience itself without reasoning cannot be known
errors.why: The Tibetan says omniscience is likewise not the criterion by which (the authority) is to be known; the English turns it into a claim that omniscience cannot be known without reasoning.

note: Root verses of PV II (insects, far-seeing, heya/upādeya) are correctly identified, but the dense argument around them is rendered loosely in places.

errors.english: Even in this recitation, there is no need to doubt that the procedure differs from moving it from its location.
errors.why: The Tibetan says that even in this reading one should not suspect the offence arises by a procedure other than moving from the place; the English asserts that the procedure does differ.

fix.find: there is no need to doubt that the procedure differs from moving it from its location
fix.replace: one should not suspect that the offence arises by any procedure other than moving it from its location

errors.english: If it is possible to distinguish individual ribs [note: of a structure or frame] and one moves them into another's possession
errors.why: གཞན་གྱི་བར་དུ means into the place/space of another (spoke), continuing the spoke-by-spoke discussion of the previous side, not into another person's possession.

note: Generally follows the theft (pārājika) commentary on location, growth and uprooting, but one key sentence is inverted and the opening is misconstrued.
Faithful translation of the Vigrahavyāvartanī verses and autocommentary on the regress of pramāṇas, with verses correctly set off.

errors.why: ངེས་པར་བཟུང་བ is avadhāraṇa, the restrictive particle/restriction (eva), not an 'ascertainment' (niścaya).

note: A careful rendering of a difficult passage on the conventional establishment of prāmāṇya; argument structure is preserved.

errors.english: this refers to the formal procedure consisting of the motion and the fourfold action
errors.why: གསོལ་བ་དང་བཞིའི་ལས is the jñapticaturtha-karman, an act with the motion as the fourth item (motion plus three proclamations), not a motion plus a fourfold act.

fix.find: the formal procedure consisting of the motion and the fourfold action
fix.replace: the formal act with the motion as the fourth (jñapticaturtha-karman), i.e. a motion and three proclamations

note: Sound translation of the commentary on the tenth saṃghāvaśeṣa and the next rule, apart from the name of the formal act.

errors.english: If even a novice can be content
errors.why: The sentence continues the Buddha's 'one like me, of tender flesh and young' from the previous side; he is speaking of himself, not of a novice.

fix.find: If even a novice can be content
fix.replace: If even one like me, tender and young, can be content

errors.english: If you accept this, it will violate the training rule.
errors.why: Ānanda is thinking about himself: 'if I accept it'.

errors.english: [note: original: "gtan pa drubs", referring to the formal conclusion of the Kathina period]
errors.why: Spreading/making the kaṭhina is what puts the kaṭhina privileges in force (so the ten-day limit is suspended); it is not the conclusion of the period.

note: Narrative and word-glosses on the first niḥsargika are mostly right, but two speakers are wrong and the kaṭhina note misleads.

errors.english: violating close relatives and those who perform religious duties
errors.why: རིམ་གྲོ་བྱས་པ refers to those who have rendered one service or honour (benefactors), alongside relatives by marriage, not to people performing religious duties.

note: Accurate account of the hell punishments for sexual misconduct; only a minor misreading in the closing list.
Faithful translation of MMK 25.4-10 with commentary; verses and objection/response structure are preserved.
